documents.title: Georgia State University Artificial Intelligence Policy
documents.summary: University-wide AI policy covering academic and operational use by faculty, staff and students. It sets data, disclosure, tool-vetting and misuse principles, and leaves classroom AI use to the instructor.
documents.stance_why: The policy itself sets no default for student coursework: it says 'Class use of AI tools shall be at the discretion of the instructor', so it hands the decision to instructors.

units.why: The purpose statement sets the policy's aim: 'a framework for the responsible and ethical integration of AI technologies'. It is a university-level framework statement, so P56, not a stance type.
units.anchor: a framework for the responsible and ethical integration of AI technologies

units.why: Scope sentence: the policy 'applies to all Georgia State University faculty, staff, and students'. Defines who is bound, so P56 scope.
units.anchor: applies to all Georgia State University faculty, staff, and students

units.why: Principle 8 says that where AI is used 'such use shall be appropriately disclosed and transparent'; a disclosure duty on all users, so P24.
units.anchor: such use shall be appropriately disclosed and transparent
units.frag_start: In circumstances where AI is used

units.why: Principle that AI interacting with humans 'should disclose that its outputs or responses are machine-generated'. Disclosure of AI-ness, nearest type P24 (disclosure), though it binds tools/deployers.
units.anchor: should disclose that its outputs or responses are machine-generated
units.frag_start: AI interacting directly with humans should
units.policy: AI that interacts directly with humans should disclose that its outputs or responses are machine-generated.

units.why: Principle 5 'Periodically reviewing results with stakeholders to ensure AI is successfully meeting objectives' is a review commitment, P54.
units.anchor: Periodically reviewing results with stakeholders to ensure AI is successfully meeting objectives

units.why: Principle 1, 'Protecting and preserving the safety of humans', is a high-level guiding principle for AI adoption, P56.
units.anchor: Protecting and preserving the safety of humans

units.why: Members are 'expected to uphold the highest standards of integrity and foster honest scholarship, including the ethical use of emerging technologies': a principle for all, P56.

units.why: A tool not on the list requires a 'request for review to the University AI Committee'. Still a vetted-tool rule, P50.

units.anchor: responsible for the administration of this Policy
